answer: Submission rate is limited to 3 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole farm from one uplink. An operator running many aliases hence pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the pulse quota and the lantern admission check. Because the counters live in the ripple ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
